text:
ana: quick report from today's soak: when the gateway preempts long-lived streams we lose a useful UX signal. previous proposals talk about resume tokens or control frames, but those either force state or push big tokens around.

kris: agreed. tokens + state both have costs. what's your thought?

ana: (lol it's ana :wave:) thinking of a middle ground: a compact, append-only progress watermark that the gateway mirrors to a bounded ringbuffer in the control plane. not full KV for every token, just a tiny watermark per stream that's cheap to emit and cheap to retain.

tom: ringbuffer mirror? explain the flows.

ana: flow sketch: model writes small checkpoints periodically (e.g., every 64 tokens) as 32-byte watermarks: {offset, checksum, variant, short-hash}. those are emitted as tiny control-frames inline (or trailers) and the gateway mirrors only the watermark (not the token payload) to a tenant-scoped ringbuffer for ttl (default 20s). no kv cache per token, only one small object per checkpoint.

priya: so this is not a full resume-state; it's a hint we can use to validate a stateless resume token or to pick a good replay point. cheaper than storing full kv. I like it.

kris: how is this different than previous stateless token proposals?

ana: two differences: 1) we avoid large signed tokens by emitting tiny checkpoints the gateway keeps short-lived (bounded mem), 2) on resume the client sends a compact resume intent header and the gateway consults the ringbuffer to find the nearest checkpoint and route to a resume handler or fallback. improves success-rate vs purely stateless replay.

tom: nice. so in practice: model emits control-frame: `{"_rw_wm":{"o":640,"cs":"a1b2","v":1}}` and gateway mirrors `{evict_id -> wm}` into ringbuffer. if eviction happens, gateway can return `x-rw-evict-wm: a1b2;offset=640;ttl=20` instead of a huge token. client retries with `x-rw-resume-wm: a1b2`.

priya: tradeoffs: still some control-plane state but bounded: ringbuffer size = checkpoint_rate * ttl * concurrency. admission control via tenant mb-seconds trivial because objects are tiny. we also get better resume-hit rates than pure stateless tokens.

kris: what about correctness on model upgrades / variant mismatch? watermark carries variant id so gateway can detect mismatch and fall back. also useful for canary rollbacks.

ana: security: watermark contains only short-hash & offset, no prompt content. rotate mirror signing keys nightly. control-plane ringbuffer entries are tenant-scoped and opaque to other tenants.

tom: billing/metrics: add `edge.wm.issued`, `edge.wm.mirrored`, `edge.wm.resume_hit`, `edge.wm.resume_miss`, `edge.wm.fallbacks`. charge mirror storage as a tiny add-on per mb-second equivalent (very small). detect hotspots.

priya: API contract: inline control chunk for HTTP/1 fallback, trailers for HTTP/2+. sample inline chunk: 
```
{"_rw_wm":{"o":640,"cs":"a1b2c3d4","v":1}}
```
trailer sketch: 
```
x-rw-wm-offset: 640
x-rw-wm-checksum: a1b2c3d4
x-rw-wm-ttl: 20
grpc-status: 8
```

kris: client flow: if `x-rw-wm-*` or inline `_rw_wm` present -> UI shows partial + Resume if desired. retry sends `x-rw-resume-wm: a1b2c3d4`. gateway looks up mirror ringbuffer: if hit -> route to resume at that checkpoint; if miss -> fallback to short-answer variant and set `x-rw-resume-fallback:true`.

ana: implement notes: model container needs lightweight checkpoint emitter (small binary write). gateway mirror component batches mirrors to reduce IO and evicts old entries with TTL. ringbuffer per-region per-tenant to avoid cross-region latency.

tom: tests: chaos harness to inject preempt after random offsets; assert resume_hit_rate > baseline stateless; fuzz variant mismatch and TTL expiry; verify no prompt leakage.

priya: runbook & alerts: `WM_FALLBACK_RATE > 3% for 10m` and `WM_STORE_UTIL > 85%`. if high, either increase TTL or checkpoint interval. also expose `wm.mirror.size_per_tenant` to customer.

kris: rollout: behind FF `edge.wm.v1`. default off. start internal tenants -> canary -> public opt-in. docs for SDK: ResumeManager support for `wm` headers.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued: gateway/edge-proxy v1.51.0 -> canary (us-west-2) :rocket:

ana: I'll draft RFC: "Progress watermarks + mirrored ringbuffer" with schema, mirror internals, admission accounting, and SDK hooks. will ping @sdk-team and @billing.

tom: small perf question: how many watermarks/sec per host do we expect? if checkpoint_every=64 tokens and avg throughput X we'll need numbers. let's add perf targets to RFC.

priya: agree. add perf target: <1KB per second per concurrent stream mirrored; ringbuffer ops should be <1ms p99.

kris: add privacy note: never include user-generated content; only short checksum fingerprint. security review required.

infra-bot: deploy started: gateway/edge-proxy v1.51.0 canary -> 1/3 hosts succeeded.

ana: RFC: https://rfc.internal/r/progress-watermark-ringbuffer (draft) — feedback welcome :eyes:
